claims.text: Integrating graphene nanoplatelets into an HEA matrix will reduce its coefficient of friction.
Integrating graphene nanoplatelets into an HEA matrix will reduce its wear rate.
The improvements will result from in situ formation of a stable, low-shear tribolayer.
A graphene-nanoplatelet volume fraction of 2–5% can be incorporated during processing or by surface impregnation with uniform dispersion.
The intervention will remain effective during sliding from approximately -50°C to 500°C at normal atmospheric pressure.
Applied shear stress will align the dispersed graphene nanoplatelets at the contact interface.
The aligned graphene nanoplatelets will form a continuous lubricious tribolayer.
During sliding, graphene nanoplatelets will shear and exfoliate to create a low-shear-strength interface.
The tribolayer will reduce direct metal-to-metal contact.
The tribolayer will smooth the contact surface and distribute the applied load.
Reduced metal-to-metal contact, surface smoothing, and load distribution will lower friction and wear.
The treated HEA is predicted to have a coefficient of friction approximately 20–30% lower than that of the untreated HEA.
The treated HEA is predicted to have a measurably lower wear rate than the untreated HEA across the tested temperature range.
Graphene-nanoplatelet agglomeration or nonuniform distribution will diminish performance by preventing formation of an effective tribolayer.
Effectiveness may diminish above approximately 500°C because this exceeds the degradation limit of graphene.
